rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports that the Jewish scholar Malik ibn al-Sayf denied that God revealed anything to any human, even Moses, after the Prophet challenged him; the verse was then revealed.
rows.anchor: مالك بن الصيف فخاصم النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: بريدة
rows.claim: Burayda reports that the Prophet said Umm al-Qura is Mecca.
rows.anchor: ام القرى مكة

rows.speaker: علي بن أسباط
rows.claim: Asked why the Prophet was called ummi, Imam Abu Jaʿfar said he was affiliated with Mecca; Umm al-Qura is Mecca and its environs include Taʾif.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أسباط قال قلت لأبي جعفر عليه السلام لم سمي النبي الأمي؟ قال نسب إلى مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī compares the command to warn Mecca and its surroundings with 26:214; a specific warning audience does not limit the Prophet’s universal mission, affirmed in 6:19, 6:90, and 7:158.
rows.anchor: لا ينافي الأمر بإنذار طائفة خاصة عموم الرسالة لجميع الناس

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن سنان
rows.claim: In one report, Imam al-Ṣadiq explains that the People of the Book concealed whatever they wished and disclosed whatever they wished.
rows.anchor: قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن سنان
rows.claim: A second version says they wrote the revelation on sheets, then exposed what they wished and hid what they wished.
rows.anchor: قال وفي رواية أخرى عنه عليه السلام قال كانوا يكتبونه في القراطيس ثم يبدون ما شاءوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī reads “the people of knowledge” as an allusion to the Imams of the Prophet’s household.
rows.anchor: أقول أهل العلم كناية عن أئمه أهل البيت عليهم السلام

words: وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًا
rows.speaker: شرحبيل بن سعد
rows.claim: Shurahbil ibn Saʿd reports that the verse concerning one who fabricates against God was revealed about ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Sarh, who fled when the Prophet entered Mecca; foster-brother ʿUthman hid him and later sought his protection.
rows.anchor: عن شرحبيل بن سعد قال نزلت في عبد الله بن أبي سرح

words: أَوْ قَالَ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ وَلَمْ يُوحَ إِلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ
rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says the clause about claiming revelation concerns Musaylima and his rhymed, oracular utterances.
rows.anchor: قال نزلت في مسيلمة فيما كان يسجع ويتكهن به

words: وَمَنْ قَالَ سَأُنزِلُ مِثْلَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima attributes the claim of producing revelation like God’s to ʿAbd Allah ibn Saʿd ibn Abi Sarh, who allegedly altered dictated phrases and apostatized.
rows.anchor: قال نزلت في عبد الله بن سعد بن أبي سرح كان يكتب للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

words: وَمَنْ قَالَ سَأُنزِلُ مِثْلَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes that the account of ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Sarh has also been transmitted through other routes.
rows.anchor: أقول وروي هذا المعنى بطرق أخرى أيضا غير ما مر

words: وَمَنْ قَالَ سَأُنزِلُ مِثْلَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: In al-Qummi’s report, Ibn Abi Sarh was ʿUthman’s foster brother and a skilled scribe; during dictation he substituted different divine names, while the Prophet said the expressions were equivalent.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال

words: وَمَنْ قَالَ سَأُنزِلُ مِثْلَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: The report says Ibn Abi Sarh apostatized, claimed Muhammad did not know what he said, and boasted he could produce revelation without correction.
rows.anchor: فارتد كافرا ورجع مكه وقال لقريش والله ما يدري محمد ما يقول

words: وَمَنْ قَالَ سَأُنزِلُ مِثْلَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: At the conquest, the Prophet ordered Ibn Abi Sarh killed; ʿUthman interceded and the Prophet spared him, later explaining that prophets do not kill by a signal; Ibn Abi Sarh became one of the amnestied Meccans.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال

words: وَمَنْ قَالَ سَأُنزِلُ مِثْلَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says versions of the account also occur in al-Kafi, Tafsir al-ʿAyyashi, and Majmaʿ al-Bayan through al-Baqir and al-Sadiq.
rows.anchor: وروي هذا المعنى في الكافي وتفسير العياشي ومجمع البيان بطرق أخرى عن الباقر والصادق

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators call the ʿIkrima and al-Suddi versions false: the phrases they say were altered do not occur in Meccan suras, apart from later-medinan material in Luqman.
rows.anchor: ذكر بعض المفسرين بعد إيراد القصة عن روايتي عكرمة والسدي إن هاتين الروايتين باطلتان

words: وَمَنْ قَالَ سَأُنزِلُ مِثْلَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Those commentators also argue that Ibn Abi Sarh returned to Islam before the conquest and may have fabricated the story of changing revelation; if the Prophet accepted his changes, that would not explain his apostasy and return.
rows.anchor: قد رجع إلى الإسلام قبل الفتح

words: وَمَنْ قَالَ سَأُنزِلُ مِثْلَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says reliable reports from al-Sadiq and al-Baqir place Ibn Abi Sarh’s episode in Medina after the Hijra; Sunni reports do not clearly place it in Mecca and may point to Medina.
rows.anchor: الروايات المعتبرة المروية عن الصادقين عليهما السلام صريحة في وقوع قصة ابن أبي سرح في المدينة بعد الهجرة

words: وَمَنْ قَالَ سَأُنزِلُ مِثْلَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects reliance on Ibn ʿAbbas’s sura-order report to disprove a Medinan setting, judging it no stronger than the reports its critics dismiss.
rows.anchor: وأما ما استند إليه من رواية ابن عباس في ترتيب نزول السور القرآنية فليس بأقوى اعتبارا

words: وَمَنْ قَالَ سَأُنزِلُ مِثْلَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against the claim that Ibn Abi Sarh returned before the conquest, al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī cites reports from both routes: he returned only at the conquest, after ʿUthman interceded when his blood had been declared forfeit.
rows.anchor: فقد عرفت ورود الرواية من الطريقين أنه لم يعد إلى الإسلام إلى يوم الفتح

words: وَمَنْ قَالَ سَأُنزِلُ مِثْلَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He finds the verse’s wording about someone claiming “I will produce the like” not clearly matched by the reports’ wording of Ibn Abi Sarh’s boast.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى { ومن قال سأنزل مثل ما أنزل الله } غير ظاهر الانطباق

words: وَمَنْ قَالَ سَأُنزِلُ مِثْلَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Medinan date for 6:93 conflicts with its evident connection to what follows; if it is Medinan, the next two verses most likely are as well.
rows.anchor: لو كان نازلا بالمدينة كان الأقرب أن تكون الآيتان جميعا مدنيتين

words: وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًا
rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima reports another occasion: after al-Nadr ibn al-Harith parodied the opening of al-Mursalat with rhymed phrases, the verse about fabricating against God was revealed.
rows.anchor: رواه عبد بن حميد عن عكرمة قال لما نزلت والمرسلات عرفا فالعاصفات عصفا

rows.speaker: سلام
rows.claim: Salam reports from Imam al-Baqir that “the punishment of humiliation” means thirst on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: عن سلام عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله { اليوم تجزون عذاب الهون } قال العطش يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: الفضيل
rows.claim: Al-Fudayl reports the same interpretation, thirst, from Imam al-Sadiq.
rows.anchor: ورواه أيضا عن الفضيل عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام وفيه قال العطش

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A report from al-Sadiq describes Adam’s creation from two handfuls of clay gathered from the heavens and earth: the right-hand portion was destined for prophets, believers, and the honored; the left for tyrants, polytheists, hypocrites, and the wretched.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال إن الله عز وجل لما أراد أن يخلق آدم بعث جبرئيل

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: In the clay tradition, the two portions are mixed: grain signifies believers’ clay, loved by God, while the kernel signifies disbelievers’ clay, which has distanced itself from good and truth.
rows.anchor: النوى طينة الكافرين الذين نأوا عن كل خير

words: يُخْرِجُ ٱلْحَيَّ مِنَ ٱلْمَيِّتِ وَمُخْرِجُ ٱلْمَيِّتِ مِنَ ٱلْحَيِّ
rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: The report identifies the living drawn from the dead as a believer emerging from disbelievers’ clay, and the dead drawn from the living as a disbeliever emerging from believers’ clay; mixing and later separation explain death and life.
rows.anchor: فالحي المؤمن الذي يخرج من طينة الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī classifies the grain-and-kernel interpretation as inward rather than apparent meaning, notes that other reports give it too, and defers discussion of the clay traditions.
rows.anchor: الرواية من أخبار الطينة وسيجيء البحث فيها فيما يناسبه من المحل

rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي بن بنت إلياس
rows.claim: Al-Hasan ibn ʿAli ibn Bint Ilyas reports from al-Rida that God made night and women sources of repose; the Sunnah includes marrying at night and feeding people.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن بن علي بن بنت إلياس قال سمعت أبا الحسن الرضا عليه السلام يقول إن الله جعل الليل سكنا

rows.speaker: علي بن عقبة
rows.claim: ʿAli ibn ʿUqba reports from his father and al-Sadiq: marry at night because God made it repose, and do not seek one’s needs at night.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن عقبة عن أبيه عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال تزوجوا بالليل فإن الله جعله سكنا

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: A report from Abu al-Hasan says prophets were created as prophets and believers as believers, while faith was entrusted to some people and may either be completed or withdrawn; it applies the verse to these categories and says a denier of the Imams lost his entrusted faith.
rows.anchor: عن بعض أصحابنا عن أبي الحسن عليه السلام قال إن الله خلق النبيين على النبوة فلا يكونون إلا أنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes many Ayyashi and Qummi reports interpret the terms as two kinds of faith; this report treats that sense as an application of the verse.
rows.anchor: وهذه الرواية توجهها بأنها من الجري والانطباق

rows.speaker: سعد بن سعيد الأصبغ
rows.claim: Saʿd ibn Saʿid al-Asbagh reports from al-Sadiq that the settled person is in the womb and the entrusted one in the loins; faith too may be entrusted and later removed.
rows.anchor: عن سعد بن سعيد الأصبغ قال سمعت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: سدير
rows.claim: Sudayr reports that al-Baqir explained “Originator of the heavens and earth” as God originating all things by His knowledge without a prior model, and creating heavens and earth when none existed before; he cites 11:7.
rows.anchor: عن سدير قال سمعت حمران يسأل أبا جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن سنان
rows.claim: Ibn Sinan reports from al-Sadiq that “sight cannot reach Him” means mental apprehension cannot encompass God, not that eyes fail to see; “blindness” likewise means intellectual blindness, and God is too exalted for bodily sight.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن سنان عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the same interpretation is transmitted in al-Tawhid through another route from al-Sadiq and from Abu Hashim al-Jaʿfari through al-Rida.
rows.anchor: أقول ورواه في التوحيد بطريق آخر عنه عليه السلام وبإسناده عن أبي هاشم الجعفري عن الرضا

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الرضا
rows.claim: In a debate reported by Safwan ibn Yahya, Abu Qurra claims that vision was assigned to Muhammad and speech to Moses; al-Rida challenges how Muhammad could transmit that God is unseen and then claim to see Him bodily.
rows.anchor: قال أبو قرة إنا روينا أن الله قسم الرؤية والكلام بين نبيين فقسم الكلام لموسى ولمحمد الرؤية

rows.speaker: الرضا
rows.claim: Al-Rida says Muhammad saw God’s signs, not God Himself; seeing God would entail encompassing Him in knowledge, contrary to the verse, and he rejects reports that oppose the Qur’an and Muslim consensus.
rows.anchor: فآيات الله غير الله وقد قال الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says other reports affirm a more subtle kind of vision fitting God’s sanctity, to be discussed under al-Aʿraf; the report rejects bodily sight because that was the common view and reason and scripture disprove it.
rows.anchor: وهناك روايات أخر تثبت الرؤية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Tabari transmits from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that the Prophet saw his Lord; when challenged with this verse, ʿIkrima analogized seeing God to seeing the sky.
rows.anchor: في تفسير الطبري عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the reported vision is bodily vision by the seeing organ, which reason and transmitted revelation deny.
rows.anchor: والذي تثبته من الرؤية صريح الرؤية الجسمانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the verse only denied seeing every side of an object, it would say nothing distinctive about God: ordinary sight perceives only the surfaces facing its beam, never all sides of any body.
rows.anchor: في هذا السنخ من الإدراك البصري المحال فيه وفي غيره

rows.speaker: إسماعيل بن الفضل
rows.claim: Asked whether God is seen in the hereafter, al-Sadiq says sight apprehends only what has color and modality, while God creates colors and modalities.
rows.anchor: عن إسماعيل بن الفضل قال سألت أبا عبد الله جعفر بن محمد الصادق عليه السلام عن الله تبارك وتعالى هل يرى في المعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī gives “established you on earth” as settling and placing people there; it may instead mean empowering and granting control, supported by the parallel in 2:29.
rows.anchor: أي جعلنا مكانكم الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Means of living” is the plural of maʿisha: whatever sustains life, such as food, drink, and similar necessities.
rows.anchor: والمعايش جمع معيشة وهي ما يعاش به من مطعم أو مشرب أو نحوهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reminds humanity of the blessing of inhabiting or controlling the earth and its livelihoods, hence the rebuke that people give little thanks.
rows.anchor: والآية في مقام الامتنان عليهم بما أنعم الله عليهم من نعمة سكنى الأرض أو التسلط والاستيلاء عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation and prostration account begins here and extends fifteen verses, expanding the previous verse’s summary and explaining how humanity came to be established on earth; the oath-like lām marks its opening.
rows.anchor: صورة قصة تبتدئ من هذه الآية إلى تمام خمس عشرة آية يفصل فيها إجمال الآية السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prostration and Garden episodes are presented as one connected story, ending with the decree of descent and earthly settlement, so the detailed story matches 7:10’s summary.
rows.anchor: سيقت القصتان أعني قصة الأمر بالسجدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address “We created you then fashioned you” is to all humanity and is an address of blessing, as in the preceding verse; it restates the same substance in fuller detail.
rows.anchor: الخطاب فيه لعامة الآدميين وهو خطاب امتناني كما مر نظيره في الآية السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ prostration was for all human descendants, with Adam as the appointed direction and representative of humanity, not the object because of his individual person; the Kaaba similarly directs worship toward lordship.
rows.anchor: السجدة كانت من الملائكة لجميع بني آدم أي للنشأة الإنسانية وإن كان آدم عليه السلام هو القبلة المنصوبة للسجدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The satanic influence on human beings reaches their consciousness and practical thought: their representations of things and judgments about what should or should not be done.
rows.anchor: والثانية أن الذي يمسه الشيطان من بني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madhʾum means blamed or reproached, from dhamm; madhur means expelled and driven away in humiliation, from dahr.
rows.anchor: المذؤوم من ذامه يذامه ويذيمه إذا عابه وذمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in “whoever follows you” is an oath, answered by “I will surely fill Hell”; the divine response matches Iblis’s threat concerning humanity.
rows.anchor: اللام للقسم وجوابه هو قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From you” includes Iblis and his followers in the punishment, while its partitive wording means that God does not say every human being followed him.
rows.anchor: أي منك ومنهم فأشركه في الجزاء معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam alone is directly addressed, while his wife is included in the ruling.
rows.anchor: خص بالخطاب آدم عليه السلام وألحق به في الحكم زوجته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission to eat wherever they wished broadly allows their use of the Garden, except for the tree singled out next.
rows.anchor: توسعة في إباحة التصرف إلا ما استثناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their “wronging” themselves means self-harm, not disobedience to a binding legislative command, since the prohibition was guidance.
rows.anchor: والظلم هو الظلم على النفس دون معصية الأمر المولوي فإن الأمر إرشادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waswasa is a call or invitation to something in a quiet voice.
rows.anchor: الوسوسة هي الدعاء إلى أمر بصوت خفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muwara is hiding something by placing it behind what conceals it; sawʾat are body parts a person is ashamed to expose.
rows.anchor: المواراة ستر الشيء بجعله وراء ما يستره

words: إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَٰلِدِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī reads Satan’s claim as saying God forbade the tree only because He disliked their becoming angels or immortal.
rows.anchor: أي إلا كراهة أن تكونا ملكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even when malak (“angel”) has fatḥa on the lām, al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says it carries the sense of malik (“king”), supported by 20:120’s “kingdom that does not decay.”
rows.anchor: والملك وإن قرئ بفتح اللام إلا أن فيه معنى الملك

rows.speaker: السيد المرتضى
rows.claim: Al-Murtada’s alternative is that Satan made them think only angels, not humans, were forbidden the tree, deepening their confusion; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects it because 20:120 points otherwise.
rows.anchor: ونقل في المجمع عن السيد المرتضى رحمه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqasama conveys emphatic oath-taking: Satan swore solemnly that he was their sincere adviser; sincerity is the opposite of deceit.
rows.anchor: المقاسمة المبالغة في القسم أي حلف لهما وأغلظ في حلفه أنه لهما لمن الناصحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadliya means bringing near or delivering; tadalli is approaching or letting oneself down, metaphorically from lowering a bucket; ghurur is feigned advice concealing deceit.
rows.anchor: التدلية التقريب والإيصال كما أن التدلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khasf means joining and gathering, as in patching a shoe.
rows.anchor: الخصف الضم والجمع، ومنه خصف النعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later call and “that tree” indicate distance from God and the tree; at their first arrival, God said “this tree,” indicating nearness.
rows.anchor: دلالة على أنهما عند توجه هذا الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their confession is complete humility and supplication: rather than asking for a particular favor, they declare their need for forgiveness and mercy and their looming loss.
rows.anchor: هذا منهما نهاية التذلل والابتهال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address appears to include Adam, his wife, and Iblis; their mutual enmity is seen in their differing natures, and the earthly dwelling and provision last until worldly life ends.
rows.anchor: كأن الخطاب لآدم وزوجته وإبليس

words: فِيهَا تَحْيَوْنَ وَفِيهَا تَمُوتُونَ وَمِنْهَا تُخْرَجُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This decree ties them to earth until resurrection; the address probably includes Adam, his wife, and their descendants, as a new “He said” introduces it.
rows.anchor: قضاء آخر يوجب تعلقهم بالأرض إلى حين البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī refers readers to his fuller discussion of the Garden story in the commentary on al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وقد مر تفصيل الكلام في قصة الجنة في سورة البقرة فليراجعها من شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author introduces a discussion of Satan, criticizing casual cursing and attribution of bad thoughts to him without reflection on the Qur’an’s account of this unseen being and his influence over human life.
rows.anchor: دون أن نتدبر فنحصل ما يعطيه القرآن الكريم في حقيقة هذا الموجود العجيب الغائب عن حواسنا
